source_metadata.exact_title: Human-to-Dog Transmission of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus
source_metadata.source_type: journal dispatch / household case report with outbreak context

atoms.canonical_statement: During the 2003 nursing-home outbreak, 48 patients and 15 nurses were identified as MRSA carriers, and most outbreak isolates belonged to PFGE RIVM cluster 35.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During a large outbreak in 2003 ... 48 patients and 15 nurses were identified as carriers of MRSA

population.label: 2003 nursing-home MRSA carriers (48 patients and 15 nurses)

atoms.canonical_statement: A 31-year-old nurse with psoriasis was identified as an MRSA carrier during the 2003 nursing-home outbreak.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In 2003, a 31-year-old female nurse who had psoriasis was identified as an MRSA carrier

atoms.canonical_statement: The nurse initially received intranasal mupirocin plus chlorhexidine-in-ethanol washing for 7 days to eliminate MRSA carriage.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: applying mupirocin ointment in her nares and washing with a chlorhexidine in ethanol solution for 7 days

atoms.canonical_statement: After initial decolonization the nurse became MRSA-negative, but later MRSA was again isolated from her nose, throat, perineum, and skin lesions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Initially she became MRSA-negative but later converted to a carrier state again

atoms.canonical_statement: The nurse was treated for psoriatic skin lesions with topical triamcinolone acetonide/tetracycline and then received oral doxycycline plus rifampin for MRSA carriage.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: treated for her psoriasis with topical application of triamcinolonacetonide/tetracycline ... oral doxycycline and rifampin

exposures.details: applied to minimize psoriatic skin lesions

atoms.canonical_statement: Despite the second treatment sequence, the nurse again became colonized at all previously positive sites after several weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, after some weeks, she became colonized again at all previously mentioned sites.

atoms.canonical_statement: Household screening found MRSA in the 1-year-old daughter at the nose, throat, and skin lesions and in the healthy dog at the nares but not the perineum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: her 1-year-old daughter ... was colonized in the nose, throat, and skin lesions. The nares ... of their healthy pet dog were also colonized.

population.label: Household contacts: 1-year-old daughter and healthy pet dog

atoms.canonical_statement: The husband and the child's grandmother had negative MRSA screening cultures at the sampled sites.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Samples ... from the patient’s husband were MRSA negative, as were samples ... of the baby’s grandmother

population.label: Household contacts with negative screening: husband and grandmother

atoms.canonical_statement: Staphylococci from the nurse, child, and dog were identified as S. aureus by conventional methods, Vitek 2, and a tuf-targeting PCR assay.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: identified as S. aureus by conventional methods, Vitek 2 ... and Martineau polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which targets the tuf gene

atoms.canonical_statement: All three isolates were reported resistant to penicillin G, ofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and fusidic acid, while disk diffusion showed mupirocin susceptibility.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: isolates were resistant to penicillin G, ofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and fusidic acid ... Disk diffusion ... susceptibility to mupirocin

population.label: MRSA isolates from nurse, child, and dog

atoms.canonical_statement: An oxacillin screening agar containing 6 µg/mL oxacillin and 4% NaCl showed no growth after 24 or 48 hours at 35°C.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: oxacillin screening test ... 6 µg/mL ... showed no growth after 24 h and 48 h of incubation at 35°C

atoms.canonical_statement: By Etest, the dog and child MRSA isolates each had an oxacillin MIC of 6 mg/L.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the isolates of the dog and the baby had an oxacillin MIC of 6 mg/L

quantitative_result.original_result_text: dog and baby oxacillin MIC 6 mg/L

atoms.canonical_statement: By Etest, the nurse MRSA isolate had an oxacillin MIC of 4 mg/L.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the isolate from the nurse had an oxacillin MIC of 4 mg/L

atoms.canonical_statement: PBP2 slide latex agglutination was positive for the nurse, child, and dog isolates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a PBP2 slide latex agglutination test ... was positive for all three isolates

population.label: MRSA isolates from nurse, child, and dog

atoms.canonical_statement: mecA PCR was positive for all three isolates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: presence of the mecA gene ... was demonstrated by a positive mecA PCR for all three isolates

population.label: MRSA isolates from nurse, child, and dog

atoms.canonical_statement: SCCmec characterization used ccrA/B typing, mec-complex typing, and PCR detection of structural variants across the genetic element.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Characterization ... was performed by typing the ccrA/B gene complex, the mec complex, and ... a PCR strategy

atoms.canonical_statement: SCCmec typing of the dog and owner isolates appeared identical: ccrA/B gene type 4, mec complex class B, with none of loci A-H detected.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: seemed to be identical (ccrA/B gene type 4, mec complex class B, and no loci A-H were found)

atoms.canonical_statement: PFGE was performed using the method of Schwarzkopf and colleagues to compare the household MRSA isolates with the nursing-home outbreak cluster.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: PFGE was carried out as described by Schwarzkopf et al.

atoms.canonical_statement: PFGE showed indistinguishable patterns for the dog, child, and nurse isolates; all belonged to RIVM cluster 35, the same cluster seen in the nursing-home outbreaks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: all three MRSA isolates ... had indistinguishable patterns and ... belonged to RIVM cluster 35

population.label: MRSA isolates from dog, child, and nurse

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors inferred that the dog acquired the same strain as the owner through contact, but they could not determine whether the dog, child, or an unknown nursing-home source reinfected the nurse.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we assume that the dog became colonized with the same strain as its owner through contact ... either the dog or the baby or an unknown source ... reinfected the nurse

atoms.canonical_statement: For the final coordinated treatment, the mother and dog received oral doxycycline plus rifampin, while the child received clarithromycin plus rifampin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the mother and the dog received an oral course of doxycycline and rifampin; the baby was treated with clarithromycin and rifampin

exposures.details: given to mother, child, and dog

atoms.canonical_statement: The coordinated treatment was followed by elimination of MRSA from the mother, child, and dog.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This treatment finally eliminated MRSA from the mother, the child, and the dog.

atoms.canonical_statement: Follow-up cultures remained negative for 2 months in the dog and child and for 9 months in the mother.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Follow-up cultures from the dog and the child were taken for 2 months, the mother was monitored for 9 months, and all cultures remained negative.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors described this as the first known case of human-to-animal MRSA transmission in the Netherlands.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report the first known case of human-to-animal transmission of MRSA in the Netherlands.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors proposed that the household MRSA SCCmec pattern was unclassifiable in the then-current system and might represent a new SCCmec type.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: this MRSA cannot be classified in the current system and may present a new SCCmec type

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors noted that Vitek 2 and the oxacillin screening test failed to identify these low-level oxacillin-resistant mecA-positive isolates as MRSA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the Vitek 2 did not detect MRSA in our study ... The oxacillin-screening test also did not detect our MRSA strains

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors stated that mecA PCR remained the most reliable procedure for MRSA detection and recommended mecA testing when fluoroquinolone-resistant S. aureus is encountered.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The most reliable procedure for detecting MRSA remains the PCR amplification of the mecA gene ... should be tested for the presence of the mecA gene by PCR.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that close-contact pets can become MRSA-colonized and may contribute to otherwise unexplained recurrent human carriage or infection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: dogs and other pets living in close contact with human MRSA carriers can become colonized with MRSA ... recurrent MRSA colonization or infection in humans

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors advocated simultaneous antimicrobial treatment of affected healthcare workers, human household carriers or infections, and colonized pets, with systemic rather than topical treatment for pets.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Antimicrobial therapy of healthcare workers and, at the same time, of MRSA carriers and any infected family members or pets ... Pets should be treated systemically
